To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the release rate of the drug from the coated resin particles was affected by the particle size and coating level, but the mechanical strength of polymer was a critical factor in the manufacturing process.

the drug release from resin matrix was controlled by the diffusion of drug through the matrix, and the release profiles of the resin complex were not affected significantly by compression into the tablets when the coating polymer had a higher mechanical strength.

the release rates of drug from the resin complex can be modulated by the particle size of resin and the level of polymer coating, and that the mechanical properties of polymers are critical to maintain the integrity of the coating during the manufacturing processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new sustained-release FDTs using ion-exchange resin complexes and various polymer coating materials.
developing sustained-release FDTs using ion-exchange resin complex with different polymer-coated particles.
a new sustained-release FDT formulation, which is prepared by coating drug-ion-exchange resin complex with an aqueous polymeric dispersion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sustained-release FDTs can be prepared by coating ion-exchange resin-drug complex with suitable polymer.
the sustained release FDTs can be successfully developed by using ion-exchange resin-drug complexes coated with aqueous polymeric dispersion.
the drug loading and sustained release of FDTs could be controlled by the particle size of the resins and the coating level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the drug release rate can be controlled by the particle size of the ion-exchange resin, the coating level, and the type of coating polymer, and the drug release mechanism can be described using the Boyd model and Higuichi equation.
the ion-exchange resin can be used as a drug carrier for the sustained-release FDTs and the coating of the resin particles can be achieved using various aqueous polymer dispersions.
the drug release rate can be controlled by changing the particle size of the resin, coating level, and polymer properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ion-exchange resin complexes could be used to prepare sustained-release FDTs by coating the particles with appropriate polymers.
the combination of ion-exchange resin and fast-disintegrating tablet formulation can be a useful tool for the development of sustained-release fast-disintigrating tablets (SRTs).
the drug loading and drug release profiles of ion-exchange resin complexes can be controlled by the particle size of the ion-exchange resin.
